title: EntertainmentCo
fit_question: Can you describe a time when you had to work with a difficult stakeholder on a project? What was the situation, how did you handle it, and what was the outcome?
prompt: EntertainmentCo is the world's largest live entertainment company, with two distinct business divisions—a ticketing division and a venue management division. Due to an anticipated crackdown from federal regulators, EntertainmentCo is planning a spin-off of its ticketing division. Your client is a PE firm that is interested in investing in the spin-off. Should they do it?

clarifying_info.answer: The PE firm specializes in telecommunications, media and entertainment. It targets 50% increases in both revenue and EBITDA from initial investment in year 1 to exit in year 5 and can invest $175 million in operational improvements.
It markets, prices, sells and distributes tickets online, by phone and at physical box offices, manages inventory, provides customer support and ensures ticket validity.
It promotes and produces concerts, theater and sports events for artists, performers and teams.
Press and entertainment-media attention has raised antitrust concerns: events organized by the venue division must use the proprietary ticket platform, weakening competition.

interviewer_notes: Tests revenue, EBITDA and connecting exhibits; suggested after 15–20 cases. Ask for exact ticketing revenue before permitting rounding to $500m. The source instructs use of $240m EBITDA later, but 66% of $360m is $237.6m, not exactly $240m. Retain $240m as the source's rounded follow-on convention and label it. Exhibit 2's revenue-category descriptions are interviewer-only and may be read aloud on request; use the candidate page109, not solution108. Project selection must respect the $175m budget and success-risk ratings. Source mixes year-1/year-5 language with 2024–2029 projections; preserve the displayed dates and year-5 project labels without inventing a timing adjustment.

suggested_framework.summary: Evaluate the spin-off's financial trajectory, improvement capabilities and competitive market.

children.label: Ticket fees × tickets and partnership fees × partners
Technology, labor, marketing, royalties and compliance costs
New events, partnerships and portfolio synergies

stages.interviewer_asks: How would you evaluate this investment?
stages.release_when: After the prompt; clarifications on request.
stages.info_to_release: The investor wants 50% revenue and EBITDA growth by exit and has up to $175m for operating improvements.
stages.expected_answer: Establish current ticketing revenue and EBITDA, compare standalone forecasts with both growth hurdles, then evaluate affordable improvement projects and post-separation business risks. Consider market demand, competition, technology and capabilities.
good_answer_signals: Asks for financial data tied to both investor objectives.

stages.interviewer_asks: What revenue and EBITDA did ticketing generate in 2024, and what are the growth targets?
stages.release_when: Show Exhibit 1. Require exact revenue first; then release the source's rounding instructions.
stages.info_to_release: Total revenue $2,268m, ticketing share 22%; total EBITDA $360m, ticketing share 66%. After exact calculation, the source instructs rounding revenue to $500m and using $240m EBITDA for subsequent calculations. Growth target is 50% for each.
stages.expected_answer: Exact ticketing revenue is $498.96m and EBITDA $237.6m. Exact 50%-growth targets are $748.44m and $356.4m. Under the explicitly rounded follow-on convention, targets are $750m revenue and $360m EBITDA. Do not call 66% exactly two-thirds. Exhibit 2 later supplies a $239m bottom-up EBITDA baseline, a separate minor inconsistency, whose exact target would be $358.5m.
good_answer_signals: Reads the color-coded ticketing shares correctly.
Distinguishes exact values from the requested rounding convention.

stages.interviewer_asks: Do the 2029 standalone projections support investing without improvements?
stages.release_when: Show candidate Exhibit 2 after establishing targets. Category details only if requested, orally.
stages.info_to_release: Exhibit 2 gives five revenue streams with 2024/2029 revenue and EBITDA. On request: service fees pay for the platform, support and operations; convenience fees apply to phone purchases; advertising sells site space/sponsorships; delivery covers physical-ticket shipping; premium services include VIP packages and meet-and-greets. Forecasts assume no operational improvements.
stages.expected_answer: Sum the rows: 2024 revenue $500m and EBITDA $239m; 2029 revenue $693m and EBITDA $335m. Increases are $193m (38.6%) and $96m (40.17%). Both fall short of 50%, whether using the bottom-up baselines or the rounded $750m/$360m targets. The status quo does not meet investment criteria; investigate operational improvements.
good_answer_signals: Adds each row rather than importing solution-page totals.
Recognizes the spin-off needs active value creation.

stages.interviewer_asks: How could the PE firm increase revenue and EBITDA?
stages.release_when: After the status-quo shortfall is identified.
stages.expected_answer: Revenue levers include new event types such as professional conferences or augmented-reality events, personalized recommendations, complementary parking/food packages, branded credit cards or data services. Cost levers include support automation, inventory improvement, renegotiated royalties/fees and less office space. Given strong ticketing margins, the source emphasizes revenue growth and limited cost-cutting room. Consider how separation changes the business model.
good_answer_signals: Offers ticketing-specific levers and recognizes post-spin-off dependencies.

stages.interviewer_asks: Which projects should the PE firm fund within $175m?
stages.info_to_release: Bundles: $25m investment, +$20m revenue, +$15m EBITDA, three-quarter-filled success indicator. Marketing data: $50m, +$20m, +$20m, three-quarter filled. New events: $100m, +$30m, +$20m, quarter filled. AI pricing: $75m, +$18m, +$15m, half filled. Benefits are year-5 figures; success indicators are qualitative, not numeric probabilities.
stages.expected_answer: Bundles + marketing data + AI pricing costs $150m and adds $58m revenue/$50m EBITDA, reaching $751m/$385m, above both rounded targets. Bundles + marketing data + new events costs $175m and adds $70m/$55m, reaching $763m/$390m. Both meet targets within budget, but the source favors the first combination because new events has low success potential; it also leaves $25m unspent. Benefits remain uncertain and are not probability-weighted forecasts.
good_answer_signals: Checks budget and both growth constraints.
Considers qualitative success risk rather than maximizing nominal benefits alone.

stages.interviewer_asks: The investing partner is about to enter. What is your recommendation?
stages.expected_answer: Invest subject to diligence and implement bundles, marketing data and AI pricing: $150m of projects can lift the year-5 forecast to $751m revenue and $385m EBITDA, clearing even the conservative rounded $750m/$360m hurdles. Consider separation-related loss of artists/venues, competitor response and forecast reliability. Conduct due diligence and finalize a bid; no acquisition price or investment-return multiple is given.
good_answer_signals: Makes the recommendation conditional on executing the improvements.
Names concrete spin-off and projection risks.

exhibits.title: Pre-spin-off revenue and EBITDA mix, 2024
exhibits.description: Revenue total $2,268m and EBITDA total $360m, with business mix shown by matching colors.
exhibits.key_insight: Ticketing generates 22% of revenue but 66% of EBITDA, indicating relatively high margins.

exhibits.title: Projected ticketing revenue and EBITDA, USD millions
exhibits.description: Candidate-facing component projections, excluding operating improvements. No calculated totals are included in the data.
exhibits.key_insight: The standalone forecast falls short of both 50% growth targets.

exhibits.title: Operational efficiency project opportunities
exhibits.description: Project investment and supplied year-5 incremental impacts, with qualitative success indicators. Bundles add travel/parking/insurance/merchandise; data supports targeted recommendations; events add conferences/virtual/VR; AI optimizes individualized pricing. Budget $175m.
exhibits.key_insight: Two feasible combinations meet targets, but lower success potential makes the new-event option riskier.

math.answer: $498.96 million; source permits subsequent rounding to $500m.
math.book_answer_if_different: Question 1 correctly gives $498.96M, but Question 2 says 'Round $494.56M to $500M'; $494.56M is a typo.

math.question: What is exact 2024 ticketing EBITDA?
math.answer: $237.6 million, approximately $240m under the book's later rounding convention.
math.book_answer_if_different: Book labels '$360M × 66% = $240M' a precise calculation and substitutes 2/3. Exact 66% gives $237.6M; Exhibit 2 separately sums to $239M.

math.question: What are the 50% growth targets?
math.answer: Exact targets $748.44m/$356.4m; use explicitly rounded $750m/$360m as the source's follow-on convention.
math.book_answer_if_different: Book targets $750M revenue/$360M EBITDA use rounded baselines, including its inaccurate claim that 66% of $360M is exactly $240M.

math.question: Does the status quo meet the targets?
What does the preferred project combination deliver?
What does the new-event alternative deliver?
math.answer: $175m investment reaches $763m revenue and $390m EBITDA, with lower new-event success potential.

synthesis: Conditionally invest and fund bundles, marketing data and AI pricing for $150m. Their modeled year-5 revenue of $751m and EBITDA of $385m clear both the exact and rounded growth hurdles. The source's 2024 EBITDA calculation is inaccurate: 66% of $360m is $237.6m, not exactly $240m; this correction does not change project selection. Validate separation-related customer losses, competitive responses and project assumptions before finalizing a bid.
what_great_looks_like: Connects business-mix, standalone-forecast and project exhibits.
Checks revenue and EBITDA targets separately.
Considers project success risk within the budget.
Recognizes dependence on the former parent may change after separation.
common_pitfalls: Using the parent company's entire revenue as the spin-off baseline.
Selecting projects on nominal upside alone.
Assuming operational budget is the acquisition purchase price.

extraction.notes: All three candidate exhibits visually reviewed and calculations recomputed in math-darden-entertainment.py, including feasible project combinations. Source errors: Question2 misprints revenue as $494.56M instead of $498.96M; Question1 calls 66%×$360M=$240M precise, but it is $237.6M. Later explicit rounding instructions to use $500M/$240M are preserved in release information, with corrected exact targets alongside. Exhibit2's EBITDA components sum to $239M, a separate minor baseline inconsistency. Project selection is unchanged across those baselines. Dates 2024–2029 conflict with loose year1-to-year5 wording. Success-fill symbols are ordinal, not calibrated probabilities. Candidate Exhibit2 page109 excludes interviewer-only details and worked totals on page108. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-10-03.
